metadata.title: I Love Smelly Food!
metadata.description:
I buy pork from a few selected rearers who live in different villages across Dima Hasao, Assam, 🇮🇳. They raise just a couple of pigs a year, and buying from them is my small way of supporting our local economy, something I deeply believe in.

The Akhuni (also known as Axone) I used is made from fermented soybeans. This one has a bit of spice, likely ginger, chilli, and garlic and I picked it up at the Saturday organic bazaar in our town Haflong. It’s imported from Nagaland, where it’s a much-loved traditional ingredient known for its strong, slightly pungent smell and deep umami flavour.

The climbing wattle leaves (Acacia pennata also known locally as Khanghu among the Mizos) have a strong, sulfur-like, oniony or garlicky smell. Some even describe it as similar to cooked rice water or slightly fermented greens. The pungency is noticeable and can be off-putting to those unfamiliar with it.
Once cooked, the pungency mellows down and gives way to a mildly bitter, earthy, and slightly nutty flavor. It pairs beautifully with eggs, fermented foods, and meat dishes in many Northeast and Southeast Asian cuisines.
The distinctive smell is part of what makes it such a loved (or hated!) ingredient. I first saw a similar recipe shared by some Indonesian food bloggers, and it’s become one of my favourites. 

Hope you enjoyed today’s simple meal and recipe stories. ❤️
